original_failure.assertion: real browser audio graph contains the PWM waveform

attempts.detail: Copy location could not resolve platform/tests-local playwright; original log retained, only diagnostic copy import corrected.

conclusions: There is no product or checked-in test source drift against the previous 113+15 PASS receipt.
The original failure is real but its harness recorded no AudioContext time, measured peak or browser/audio errors at failure, so the exact cause cannot be proven retrospectively.

The diagnostic retained the original first-read threshold and observed a nonzero waveform at 101.3ms. The audio context had advanced only 53.3ms at that wall-clock point; later samples remained nonzero.
A fresh, unchanged full audio suite then passed 113 logic assertions and 15 browser checks. This is a new run; it does not replace or relabel the earlier failure.
Fixed wall-clock sleep is sensitive to audio backend initialization and render scheduling. That is a plausible test flake mechanism, not a fully reproduced root cause from this investigation.
No concrete product audio defect or browser version regression was established. No product or checked-in test edit is justified by this evidence alone.

optional_harness_improvement.recommendation: Replace the single fixed 100ms read with bounded observation of the actual analyser waveform. Keep the same >0.001 threshold, retain all samples and context timing/state, and still fail at a finite deadline if no waveform appears.
optional_harness_improvement.purpose: Test observed audio rendering rather than assume it starts within a fixed wall-clock sleep.

limits: Headless native Web Audio browser fixture only; does not prove Device Service, guest Unit behavior, physical acoustics or a final hardware output.
No timing stress, OS audio-device changes or global browser/audio services were performed.
